title: Good COP, bad COP
transcript:
Speaker 1: ABC Listen.
Host: Podcasts, radio, news, music, and more.
Host: Want to know what's keeping ABC's business reporters busy?
Speaker 2: Who is going to lose their jobs?
Who will be benefiting from artificial intelligence?
It's an open question at the moment.
Host: Join me, Carrington Clark, host of ABC Business Daily, every Monday through Thursday, as I sit down with my fellow journalists to chat everything from markets to monetary policy.
Find ABC Business Daily on ABC Listen, or wherever you get your podcasts.
Patricia Karvelas: It was the longest cop on record, and it ended with no deal.
Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen, was president of negotiations.
So, is he responsible for the result?
And what does this failure say about the world's ability to work together on climate change and other huge issues in the future?
Back in Canberra, it's finally the last sitting week of 2026.
Controversial bills, last-minute concessions, and lots of political horse trading.
So, who's going to get what they want and who's going to be walking away empty-handed?
Welcome to Politics now.
Patricia Karvelas: Hi, I'm Patricia Karvelas.
Jacob Greber: And I'm Jacob Greber.
Welcome to the swamp.
Don't you think it feels swampy here in Canberra today?
Patricia Karvelas: You mean because of the weather?
Jacob Greber: Yeah.
Patricia Karvelas: Yeah.
Jacob Greber: Of course.
What are you thinking?
Patricia Karvelas: Well, just you just sort of swampy in its political narrative as well.
It's swampy-ish.
Yeah, the weather is revolting.
I didn't get to do my normal run, which always sets me up for the week because it was very much.
Jacob Greber: It was 91% humidity, it said on my TV.

Um, I think we can go with the swamp narrative.
Jacob Greber: Yeah, I think so.

So, cop 31 ends without a deal.
Just to give you the backstory, cop is the world's biggest climate summit.
Whole world gets together and tries to design a plan.
Um, they did attempt to talk about fossil fuels and then in the final statement, not even a mention of fossil fuels.
I think, well, there was no final statement, because no one agreed on a final statement because half the world said there's no mention of fossil fuels in the statement.
Patricia Karvelas: But that's what I mean, like in there's nothing.
Jacob Greber: Yeah.
Patricia Karvelas: No, there's nothing.
Jacob Greber: There's literally nothing.
A dissenting report.

In terms of the the it just not getting anywhere.

Yes.

Is cop even worth doing any more?
I just what is it doing?
Who's it for?
What are the outcomes?

Uh I suspect the same is true in Moscow.
